title: policy-as-code-gpu-tenant-guardrails-and-opa-admission
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This page defines Redwood's policy-as-code guardrails for GPU tenant provisioning and runtime access in Kubernetes clusters and cloud accounts. The goal is to enforce least-privilege, safe resource limits, and network egress isolation with an automated admission policy layer (OPA Gatekeeper / OPA Admission), tied into Terraform modules and CI gates.

Scope

- Applies to all new tenant provisioning workflows that attach GPU quotas, node pool labels, or network routes.
- Targets: EKS/GKE/AKS clusters that run inference runtime pods, cloud IAM and service accounts used for tenant workloads, and Terraform modules that provision tenant namespaces and nodepools.
- Exclusions: Internal system namespaces (kube-system, redwood-platform) covered by separate policies.

Motivation

- Prevent accidental over-provisioning of GPUs or granting broad cloud roles to tenant service accounts.
- Ensure network egress paths are reviewed and limited for regulated tenants.
- Shift compliance checks left into CI via policy-as-code so deployments never reach production with unsafe configs.

Design principles

1. Declarative, testable policies written in Rego and tested in CI (conftest / opa test).
2. Policy enforcement at admission time for clusters; policy checks in CI for infra PRs.
3. Policy definitions versioned alongside Terraform modules in the infra repo.
4. Fast failure with clear remediation instructions surfaced in PR checks.

High-level components

- OPA Gatekeeper constraints and ConstraintTemplates deployed to clusters.
- Terraform module: redwood/gpu-tenant (namespaces, quota objects, nodeSelector / tolerations, IAM bindings).
- CI checks: conftest/regula/terraform plan parsing + unit Rego tests.
- Monitoring & alerts: policy_violation metric emitted to Observability (Prometheus -> Grafana) per-tenant.

Policy specifications (summary)

1) GPU quota limits
- Constraint: gpu-tenant-max-gpus (per-namespace)
- Goal: limit GPUs requested via limits/requests or DevicePlugin annotations.
- Configuration (example): max_gpus = 16 for managed tenants, 4 for dev sandboxes.

2) Node pool affinity label enforcement
- Constraint: require-nodepool-label
- Goal: tenant pods must target pre-approved nodepools (label: redwood/gpu-pool in [production, shared-inference]).

3) IAM minimization for tenant service accounts
- Constraint: iam-role-binding-whitelist
- Goal: Terraform must only attach roles from a curated role-set (gpu-usage-reader, inference-executor); broad roles (Owner, Editor) are disallowed.

4) Egress gating for regulated tenants
- Constraint: egress-policy-allowed-cidrs
- Goal: deny NetworkPolicy or cloud route changes that allow egress outside approved CIDR blocks for tenants marked regulated.

5) Image provenance
- Constraint: image-registry-allowlist
- Goal: only images from approved registries (ghcr.redwood-internal, registry.redwood.ai) allowed in production clusters.

Operational thresholds and SLOs

- Admission policy enforcement uptime: 99.9% (critical).
- CI policy check pass rate: 100% for terraform plan merges to main.
- Violations detected in prod: 0 allowed; any violation triggers PagerDuty SEV2 for infra oncall if it affects resource creation.

Terraform integration pattern

- Each tenant module exposes a policy metadata block that feeds policy tests. Example usage in Terraform: 

```hcl
module "gpu_tenant_acme" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood/internal/modules/gpu-tenant.git//?ref=v1.8.0"

  tenant_id         = "acme"
  max_gpus          = 8
  allowed_nodepools = ["gpu-shared-inference", "gpu-prod-1"]
  regulated         = true
  allowed_ecr_paths = ["registry.redwood.ai/inference/acme"]
}
```

- Module outputs a test manifest under build/test-manifests/${tenant_id} that CI picks up for conftest.

- Module also emits a tfmeta file used by the CI policy scanner to map role assignments to the allowlist.

Example Terraform module metadata (table)

- name: tenant_id (string)
- max_gpus: integer (max allowed GPU devices requested)
- allowed_nodepools: list(string)
- regulated: bool
- allowed_ecr_paths: list(string)

CI / Testing workflow

1) PR to infra repo containing Terraform changes triggers the pipeline: 
   - terraform init/plan (isolated workspace)
   - tfsec + checkov for scanning (security), fail on high severity.
   - conftest run against generated manifests using Rego policies stored in /policies/gpu-tenant/*.rego.
   - opa test suite run for unit Rego tests.
2) Policy violations block the merge; the CI job prints a human-friendly remediation block with file/line and suggested patch.
3) After merge to main, a nightly policy drift scanner runs to detect drift between policy intent and live clusters.

Sample Rego constraint (Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate + Constraint)

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sdenygpuoverrequest
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sDenyGPUOverRequest
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sdenygpuoverrequest

        violation[{
          "msg": msg,
          "details": {"requested": req, "limit": limit}
        }] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          req := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].resources.requests.gpu
          limit := input.parameters.max_gpus
          req > limit
          msg := sprintf("container requests %v GPUs which exceeds max_gpus=%v", [req, limit])
        }
---
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sDenyGPUOverRequest
metadata:
  name: tenant-max-gpus
spec:
  parameters:
    max_gpus: 4
  enforcementAction: deny
```

Runbook: violation handling (oncall playbook)

- Trigger: policy_violation_alert with label policy=gpu-tenant-max-gpus or CI-blocking job failure.
- Owner (primary): infra-sre-team, secondary: eng-serving-runtime.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Triage using policy_id and affected_resource from the alert payload.
  2) If in CI: leave a blocking comment in PR with remediation (CI job auto-generates patch suggestion).
  3) If in-cluster: identify namespace and pod using the Observability dashboard (link saved as "Policy Violations").
  4) If pod has already been created by a privileged pipeline, perform an emergency revoke of the offending role or scale down the pod and re-deploy with corrected spec.
- Post-incident follow-up: open an infra ticket with root cause, annotate runway/pr responsible, and update the policy or tf module if needed.

Migration and rollout plan for clusters

1) Canary cluster (dev): Deploy Gatekeeper with enforcementAction=warn for 2 weeks and surface violations to a shared Slack channel #infra-policy.
2) Beta clusters: enforcementAction=deny for non-regulated tenants with nightly drift check for 1 month.
3) Prod clusters: phased enablement by region; start with enforcementAction=deny for nodepool labels and image allowlist, then enable gpu quota checks after 1 sprint.
4) Communication: send tenant impact notice at each phase and provide a self-service remediation guide.

Rollback strategy

- If Gatekeeper causes widespread failures, we will:
  1) Temporarily scale Gatekeeper deployment replicas to 1 and set enforcementAction=warn globally.
  2) Revert the last policy change via main -> revert PR and redeploy.
  3) If network policy constraints prevent rollback, follow emergency cluster access runbook to patch constraints via k8s API with infra oncall.

Metrics and dashboards

- policy_violation_count{policy=...,cluster=...,tenant=...} (Prometheus gauge)
- ci_policy_block_count (count of PRs blocked by policy checks)
- policy_drift_detected (daily gauge)

Recommended Grafana panels:
- Violations over time (stacked by policy)
- PRs blocked by policy (by repo and author)
- Drift delta: planned vs live GPU quota per namespace

Ownership & contacts

- Policy author: Aisha Patel (infra policy)
- Primary owner: eng-infra (infra-iam@redwood.ai)
- Secondary owners: eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre
- PagerDuty rotation: infra-oncall (SEV2 for production violations)

Appendix: CI snippets and conftest example

Example conftest test command in CI:

```bash
# generate manifests from terraform module output dir
conftest test build/test-manifests/acme --policy policies/gpu-tenant
```

Example OPA unit test structure (rego):

```rego
package test.gpu

test_max_gpus_violation {
  input := {"review": {"kind": {"kind": "Pod"}, "object": {"spec": {"containers": [{"resources": {"requests": {"gpu": 12}}}]}}}}
  not k8sdenygpuoverrequest.violation with input as input
}
```

Appendix: escalation templates (PR comment)

- Auto-block message when CI finds an issue:

"Policy check failed: {policy_id}. Summary: {short_message}. Suggested fix: see build/test-manifests/{tenant_id}/{file} and update module inputs (max_gpus / allowed_nodepools). If you believe this is a false positive open a ticket to infra-policy with the policy_id and PR link."

Notes and future work

- Investigate integrating Cloud Custodian for cross-cloud IAM enforcement where Terraform plan parsing is insufficient.
- Add tenant-specific exemptions workflow (service ticket + 2 approvers) that records lifetime and revocation timeline.
- Explore dynamic quotas enforced by an operator that adjusts tenant max_gpus based on consumed vs. reserved capacity.

References

- Gatekeeper documentation: https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/
- OPA policies repo: git@repo.redwood:/infra/policies.git
- Terraform module: git@repo.redwood:/infra/modules/gpu-tenant.git
